#Graphene $HGRAF
20 October 2026

An 8.28 km sea bridge. Saltwater. Humidity. Relentless UV.

Graphene-enhanced anticorrosion coatings are now protecting China’s Xiangshan Port bridge. According to the developer, they can double the service life of conventional coatings—potentially cutting maintenance costs and extending the life of critical infrastructure.

Today’s coverage strengthens why I’m bullish on HydroGraph’s opportunity in protective coatings.

The economics are compelling: a relatively small material addition could protect assets worth vastly more than the coating itself. Longer maintenance intervals mean fewer shutdowns, less labour and fewer expensive repairs.

HydroGraph is pursuing this market through its collaboration with Sparc, testing its Fractal Graphene in protective coating formulations.

The Chinese project has no disclosed HydroGraph involvement. For me, its significance is evidence that graphene coatings are reaching substantial infrastructure applications.

Bridges, ports, ships, pipelines and offshore structures all face the same costly enemy: corrosion.

HydroGraph still needs to turn technical progress into commercial orders. But this deployment reinforces my conviction that protective coatings could become one of its most valuable markets.

https://t.co/vEMNrn8tKQ

tweets.text:
#Uranium #Silver #Copper #Gold
⚡ DAILY METALS PULSE | 20 October 2026
Big Tech backs another nuclear project. Silver production faces operational hurdles. Copper smelters struggle to secure profitable feedstock.

☢️ URANIUM — AMAZON’S NEXT NUCLEAR MOVE

Amazon, AEP and X-energy have announced feasibility work for a proposed 960 MW nuclear project in Indiana: 12 small modular reactors near a retired coal plant.

Amazon will provide development funding and intends to buy the electricity under a long-term agreement. Construction still depends on a final investment decision.

My takeaway: another major electricity customer is putting capital behind nuclear development, strengthening the case for investment across the fuel supply chain.

🥈 SILVER — AN OVERNIGHT SUPPLY REALITY CHECK

Silvercorp reported quarterly silver production at its Ying district of approximately 900,000 oz, down 41% year-on-year following safety improvement work.

The decline was expected, and Ying finished the quarter operating at 90%. However, the separate GC mine remains suspended.

A reminder that higher silver prices cannot instantly overcome operating and permitting constraints. Spot silver gained 0.7% to around $57.48 in early Tuesday trading.

🔶 COPPER — THE PRESSURE REACHES SMELTERS

South Korea’s LS MnM is considering adjustments to concentrate purchases and production as exceptionally low processing fees squeeze profitability.

The underlying tension: smelting capacity has expanded faster than mine supply, intensifying competition for concentrate.

My watch: whether these pressures translate into actual output cuts. Tight concentrate availability and refined copper inventories can tell different stories.

🥇 GOLD — A SMALL BOUNCE, A BIG POLICY TEST

Gold edged up to around $4,145/oz early today as the dollar softened.

Markets put roughly an 82% probability on unchanged Fed rates next week, while still heavily pricing a December hike.

Oil adds another complication: Brent crossed $110 on Monday. Persistent energy inflation could keep interest-rate pressure on bullion even as geopolitical risks support demand.

👀 TODAY’S FOCUS

Investment in new nuclear capacity, disruptions to silver production and whether copper smelters actually cut output.

Follow @Swedish_Uranium for the daily pulse.

@base has led @solana in DeFi TVL for 10 straight days, the first time since 2023.

But it's not as big a deal as it sounds. Here's why:

• Base's lead comes from one app. @Morpho holds ~$4.4B of Base's $6.16B, and ~97% of Base's growth over the last 30 days ($258M of $265M) went into it.

• Solana didn't really lose money. Its TVL is down ~7%, and SOL's price is down ~6%. The tokens are still there, they're just worth less.

• Solana still holds ~3x more stablecoins ($15.8B vs $5.1B on Base). Most of it just isn't deposited in DeFi apps, so TVL doesn't count it.

So if Morpho has a bad week, Base loses its lead. And if SOL's price goes back up, Solana could take the spot back without anyone moving a dollar.

If you're earning yield on Base, check who runs your Morpho vault and how much of the yield comes from token rewards.

Next time you see a chain ranking, ask two questions. Did TVL just follow the token price? Is one app doing all the work?
